entries.proposition: Nineteen patients enrolled, ranging in age from 2 to 15 years with a median of 6.5 years.
entries.snippet: 19 (53%) enrolled, ranging in age from 2 to 15 years (median: 6.5 years; Table 1)

entries.proposition: Eligibility covered ages 1 to 30 years for DIPG and 1 to 21 years for high-grade glioma.
entries.snippet: imaging-confirmed DIPG (aged 1-30 years) or histologically confirmed HGG (1-21 years)

entries.proposition: Patients with controlled seizures on non-enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants were eligible.
entries.snippet: Patients with controlled seizures on non-enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants were eligible.

entries.proposition: The reported recommended phase 2 dose was ribociclib 170 mg per square metre on days 1 to 21 and everolimus 1.5 mg per square metre on days 1 to 28; the MTD was not reached.
entries.snippet: Thus, the RP2D was 170 mg/m2 days 1-21 for ribociclib and 1.5 mg/m2 days 1-28 for everolimus; the MTD was not reached.

entries.proposition: At dose level 3 one of six patients had a DLT (grade 3 lung infection) and none of six more in the expansion cohort.
entries.snippet: Of the six patients enrolled on dose level 3, one experienced a DLT (grade 3 lung infection). An additional six patients were enrolled on dose level 3 as an expansion cohort; none experienced a DLT.

entries.proposition: The most common grade 3 or 4 toxicities were neutropenia (33 percent), leucopenia (17 percent) and lymphopenia (11 percent); 3 patients (17 percent) needed dose reduction or came off therapy for toxicity.
entries.snippet: The most common grade 3/4 toxicities were neutropenia (33%), leucopenia (17%), and lymphopenia (11%). Three patients (17%) required dose reduction or came off therapy due to toxicity.

entries.proposition: One patient left the study before cycle 9 with grade 4 cardiac toxicity (conduction disorder, prolonged QTc, ventricular tachycardia, arrhythmia) and recovered after stopping.
entries.snippet: A third patient came off study prior to cycle 9 due to grade 4 cardiac toxicity (conduction disorder with prolonged QTc, ventricular tachycardia, and arrhythmia; no history of previously diagnosed cardiac medical conditions); this patient recovered upon discontinuation of study medications.

entries.proposition: The attributable-adverse-event table lists headache in 6 patients (33 percent) and intracranial haemorrhage in 1 (6 percent) under nervous system disorders.
entries.snippet: Nervous system disorders Headache 3 3 0 0 6 (33%) Intracranial hemorrhage 1 a 0 0 0 1 (6%)
entries.anchor: Adverse event table, nervous system rows

entries.proposition: Steady-state everolimus AUC0-24h in combination was 1.9 +/- 0.9-fold that of everolimus alone.
entries.snippet: Steady-state everolimus AUC0-24 h values when given in combination were 1.9 ± 0.9-fold higher than steady-state everolimus AUC0-24 h administered alone

entries.proposition: The authors caution that the large interpatient variability limits interpretation of the possible effect of ribociclib on everolimus exposure.
entries.snippet: However, considering the large interpatient variabilities, results should be interpreted with caution.

entries.proposition: The combination RP2D (170 and 1.5 mg per square metre) is stated to be below the single-agent RP2Ds (350 and 5).
entries.snippet: the RP2D of ribociclib and everolimus in combination (170 mg/m2 days 1-21 and 1.5 mg/m2 days 1-28) is less than respective single-agent administration (350 mg/mg2 days 1-21 and 5 mg/m2 days 1-28)

entries.proposition: The authors infer, without a control arm, that dexamethasone mouthwash was effective against mucositis, comparing with a historical incidence above 30 percent for grade 3 or 4.
entries.snippet: supporting the efficacy of dexamethasone mouthwash for mucositis prevention (compared with >30% historical incidence of everolimus-related grade 3/4 mucositis36)

entries.proposition: The table footnote says the table covers only adverse events deemed attributable to the study agents, highest grade per participant.
entries.snippet: All AEs deemed attributable to study agents; reporting only the highest grade reported per participant during study treatment.
